title: ATMOSPHERIC CHANNEL MODEL FOR EO DATA DOWNLINK USING MULTIPLE SATELLITES AND GROUND STATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a propagation channel model for the design and simulation of the EO data download at Ka- and Q-band for satellite constellations and a network of ground stations.Description: The design and optimisation of the radio link at Ka and Q band for the download of scientific data from an EO mission or a constellation requires the knowledge of the dynamic properties of the atmospheric radio channel over the sky during a pass. This is needed for the evaluation of the achievable data throughput and for the design of adaptive techniques like adaptive coding and modulation (ACM). The evolution of EO observation systems from a single satellite to a train or a constellation of different spacecrafts requires also the knowledge of the spatial and temporal characteristics of the atmospheric channel during the passes of EO satellites. In addition, due to the large amount of data volume it could be neededto perform the data download from a spacecraft by using sequentially more than one ground station during the orbit. Therefore, the channel model shall consider also this configuration in its assumptions and parametrisations. Current channel models for EO data downlink have been originally developed for the case of a satellite using a single station, so they need to be updated to take into account the temporal and spatial correlation of atmospheric propagation effects during a satellite pass and over the regions crossed during an orbit. These models have not been validated using experimental data, because of the lack of propagation measurements at Ka band or above. In the meantime new non-geostationary (NGSO) constellations data have been collected and can be used for model testing.This activity aims at developing a propagation channel model for the design and simulation of the data download of EO data at 26 and 40 GHz for the cases of : - A ground station antenna tracking at the same time the passes of several EO satellites - An EO satellite completing the download of observations, and using more than one ground station during its orbit to do so. The model shall be validated using existing data from propagation campaigns at Ka band or above using satellites in non-geostationary (i.e. LEO or MEO). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - State-of-the-art review of system requirements, channel models and NGSO propagationmeasurements, model development and testing plan - Development of channel model and preparation for testing - Model testing with experimental NGSO propagation data - Application of the new model to system test-cases - Test-case analysesDeliverables: Report, SoftwareProcurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SME  RD organisations, preferably in cooperation. title: T708-900SY ADVANCING GREENER MANUFACTURING, ASSEMBLY, INTEGRATION AND TEST PROCESSES (EXPRO+)
description: Reducing environmental impacts is now required for ESA space systems under the ESA Ecodesign Policy endorsed in October 2025, shifting the focus from impact assessment to practical ecodesign solutions implementation supporting the ESA Green Agenda 2030 greenhouse gas reduction targets.  Space systems involve specific manufacturing processes and energy-intensive testing. Previous ESA work led to the ESA Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) Database, already used by European industry. However, Manufacturing, Assembly, Integration and Test (MAIT) activities remain insufficiently covered in mission LCAs, limiting assessment reliability, especially in early phases.  This activity will therefore analyse MAIT processes, develop validated datasets for the ESA LCA Database, and identify greener technologies to reduce future mission impacts. It will build on previous TDE T824-801SY on greener MAIT processes, but also onESA LCA Database activities, and generic databases such as ecoinvent.

title: T811-906GS GROUND-BASED IMAGING SYSTEM FOR ATTITUDE DETERMINATION AND IN-ORBIT SERVICING SUPPORT OF LEO OBJECTS (EXPRO+)
description: Current technologies for retrieving attitude information of a space object are based on radar imaging, passive optical light curves or laser ranges. Radar technologies operate independently of weather conditions but require prior information about the observed target. Laser-based technologies need a target equipped with retroreflector and light curves are limited by the target angular velocity on the sky and its attitude. The slow tumbling rate of a LEO satellite, combined with the brief duration of its pass, limits the amount of data available for accurate attitude reconstruction.  Although weather-dependent, imaging technology provides a high-resolution snapshot of the observed object, showing - without prior information or additional processing - whether the target is intact and how it is oriented in space. A series of images combined with a simple model of the target will allow to accurately estimate its rotational state providing a full description of its attitude. The attitude determination will be demonstrated using simulated data.  The imaging technology can support several aspects of the space safety, it will enhance the sensitivity and the astrometric accuracy of the observation system allowing the detection of fainter objects supporting both planetary defense and space debris population model refinement. Finally, the use of direct imaging technology for the characterization of re-entry events should be evaluated.
